RapidOCR and LaMa ONNX through CUDAExecutionProvider
RapidOCR and LaMa ONNX through DmlExecutionProvider
OpenCV 5 DNN CPU fallback; OpenVINO remains an optional Intel add-on

intentionalExceptions: 2026-09-05: the EasyOCR detector is retired and its constraint and vendored sdist hash are removed. PyPI shows no release after 1.7.2 on 2024-09-24, it was the slowest and largest engine in the cascade, and RapidOCR, PaddleOCR and the OpenCV 5 DNN detector cover the same work. A config or preset that names it now fails with that sentence rather than silently selecting a different engine.

2026-08-27: the NVIDIA profile moves to the CUDA 13 channel: torch==2.13.0+cu130, torchvision==0.28.0+cu130, and onnxruntime-gpu==1.29.0. Which CUDA the default PyPI onnxruntime-gpu wheel targets is still absent from wheel metadata, so it was determined by running it: 1.29.0 loads cublasLt64_13.dll and fails to create CUDAExecutionProvider without a CUDA 13 runtime, which makes the default wheel the CUDA 13 build. Verified on an RTX 4070 SUPER (driver 610.88) with torch 2.13.0+cu130 supplying that runtime: InferenceSession(providers=['CUDAExecutionProvider']) really ran on CUDAExecutionProvider. The move closes GHSA-rrmf-rvhw-rf47 (CVE-2025-3000, torch <= 2.12.1) and leaves the cu128 lane, which cannot reach a fixed torch because cu128 Windows wheels stop at 2.11.0. Superseded 2026-09-05: see the torch 2.14.0 entry below.

Python 3.10 is no longer a supported setup target because the security-reviewed ONNX Runtime 1.25+ CPU/CUDA line and the pinned DirectML 1.24.4 line do not publish CPython 3.10 wheels; Python 3.11 is the minimum reproducible runtime.

2026-08-12: NumPy is pinned to 2.4.6, the newest 2.4.x release that supports Python 3.11; NumPy 2.5.x starts at Python 3.12, so the >=3.11 project floor is intentionally retained until a coordinated Python-floor review.

2026-09-05: every profile moves to torch==2.14.0/torchvision==0.29.0. This closes CVE-2026-65918, an out-of-bounds heap read in torchvision's GIF decoder read_from_tensor callback affecting everything through 0.28.0, which the 2026-08-27 entry recorded as carried by every lane because no fixed release existed yet. torchvision 0.29.0 and torch 2.14.0 were published 2026-09-02; cp313 win_amd64 wheels were confirmed present on both the cpu and cu130 indexes on 2026-09-05 before the pins moved. torch 2.14.0 also validates sparse-tensor invariants under torch.load(weights_only=True) (pytorch #184750), which matters here because the PyTorch LaMa rung loads a third-party big-lama.pt. Verified on the RTX 4070 SUPER (driver 610.88): the nvidia venv resolves torch 2.14.0+cu130 with torchvision 0.29.0+cu130, torch.cuda.is_available() is True, and the GPU lane still activates CUDAExecutionProvider.

2026-08-27: every profile now pins torch==2.13.0/torchvision==0.28.0. NVIDIA reaches the same pair through the cu130 index; cu128 stopped at torch 2.11.0 and stranded the NVIDIA lane two minors behind.

PaddleOCR, EasyOCR, and simple-lama remain reviewed opt-ins rather than default setup packages because their OpenCV wheel ownership or NumPy caps conflict with the primary OpenCV 5 and NumPy 2 runtime.

Native wheel hashes are not embedded in pip constraints because the supported Python, Windows, Linux, CPU, CUDA, and DirectML matrix produces different artifacts; exact versions, profile hashes, the frozen SBOM, and pip-audit evidence remain mandatory.
PyTorch and PaddlePaddle use vendor indexes whose platform-specific wheels are resolved during setup; release evidence records the reviewed index list and resolved artifact versions.

The Docker image installs the maintained CPU runtime from requirements.txt with the CPU profile constraints, including RapidOCR and ONNX Runtime for LaMa; optional PaddleOCR, EasyOCR, and PyTorch backends remain outside the container image, which is not the frozen Windows distribution.

2026-08-20: the CPU profile moves to onnxruntime 1.29.0 for its security fixes (TensorRT engine-refit path traversal, missing rank/shape validation across pooling/LSTM/QLinearConv/GridSample, DML constant-tensor byte-size validation, packed sub-byte over-copy in OrtApi::GetValue). onnxruntime-directml remains at 1.24.4, the newest DirectML wheel on PyPI: the DirectML EP is in sustained engineering and Windows ML is the forward path, so the widening gap to the CPU/GPU lines is expected, not drift.

2026-08-20: paddleocr moves to 3.7.0, which publishes PP-OCRv6 (tiny/small/medium, one 50-language model, reported +4.6% detection and +5.1% recognition over PP-OCRv5-server). The reviewed DEFAULT deliberately stays PP-OCRv5 mobile so an upgrade does not silently change model weights, latency, or memory for existing users; the v6 tiers are opt-in through --paddleocr-variant tiny|small|medium.
